## 45f08b9a5f47

**Reproduced shortcut/domain gap (A2).** The canonical program counts all cells of each nonzero color. The generator instead requires every color to be exactly one 4-connected component. Therefore “keep the single largest connected component” is extensionally identical to “keep the most frequent color” on ordinary generated scenes.

I sampled 1,000 ordinary draws in each of four bands (`None`, easy, medium, hard): 4,000 grids containing 15,436 color groups. Every group was one component, and the largest-component shortcut chose the canonical winner in 4,000/4,000 grids.

Exact canonical-valid counterexample:

```text
0000000000
0222200000
0000000000
0007770000
0007770000
0000000000
0440002222
0000000000
```

Color 2 has total frequency 8 split into two components of size 4; color 7 has one component of size 6; color 4 has size 2. The canonical Racket program keeps both color-2 components. The shortcut keeps color 7. Target `self_check` rejects the case only because color 2 has two components, which is the generator-domain restriction causing the ambiguity. Full outputs, hashes, scan counts, validator result, and command are in `checks/audits/45f08b9a5f47_counterexample.json`.

A second uncovered boundary is tie-breaking: the Racket program deterministically prefers the lower color on equal frequency, while ordinary generation enforces a strict winner and treats ties as degenerate. The connected-component shortcut is the stronger reproduced finding.

**Suggested future repair, not applied here.** Permit at least one winning color to be split across multiple components while a distractor owns the largest single component. Consider a separate valid tie profile if lower-color tie behavior is part of the intended teaching domain.

triage.reason: Retained both source-bound findings-only audits, separating accepted-input authority errors from coverage gaps on validator-rejected witnesses. Targets remain unchanged. Review claims and static evidence are retained; no blanket audit repair or admission is claimed.
